belongs_to: Chapter opening banner: the compass rose that introduces the four cardinal directions (Note for Teachers: 'Help the learners in naming the four cardinal directions')
description: A compass rose: a small cream plate with a brown border; a plus-shaped cross of two double-headed arrows; 'N' above, 'S' below, 'W' on the left, 'E' on the right (the E is printed in red, N, W and S in black). It sits at the top right of the green chapter banner on a soft yellow glow, beside the QR code and the title 'Chapter 14 Maps And Locations'. The four arrow-heads point up (N), down (S), left (W) and right (E). Nothing else is drawn on it (no intermediate directions, no degrees).

belongs_to: 'Manu is facing the rising Sun. That direction is ____. His left hand is pointing in the ____ direction. His right hand is pointing in the ____ direction. which way is west?'
description: Outdoor illustration, landscape shape with a soft irregular edge. Sky is pale blue fading to white near the horizon; one bright round white-yellow Sun with a glow in the upper middle (a little right of the picture centre) and no other cloud. Behind the field are two layers of blue-grey and teal hills. The foreground is a green grassy field. Three children: (1) Manu, the boy at the left-middle, seen from BEHIND (curly dark-brown hair, cream T-shirt, pink-purple shorts, brown sandals), standing still with BOTH arms stretched straight out sideways at shoulder height with open palms, so his body faces the Sun; as the viewer sees him, his left hand is the hand on the left of the picture and his right hand is on the right of the picture; (2) a boy at the right (orange kurta, dark-brown trousers, brown sandals, hands joined in front of the chest) and (3) a girl next to him (olive-green kurta, orange trousers, purple sandals, one hand on her hip), both facing the viewer and looking toward Manu. No compass, no direction word and no arrow is drawn inside the picture; the blanks are in the text under it.
unclear: Which of the three children is Manu is taken from the text (the boy facing the Sun, seen from behind).

belongs_to: 'Children are at a bird-watching camp. Read the clues and colour the tents in the camp accordingly.' (clues: west of the road = blue; closest to the lake = green; north of the green tent = purple; south of the lake = yellow; 'Now, draw a tent to the east of the lake.')
description: Bird's-eye illustration of a camp, a landscape rectangle (about 420 x 340 px on the page, left part of the page), north up as the compass shows. A compass rose (compass rose: a small cream plate with a brown border; a plus-shaped cross of two double-headed arrows; 'N' above, 'S' below, 'W' on the left, 'E' on the right (the E is printed in red, N, W and S in black)) is printed OUTSIDE the picture, below the clue text on the right. Parts: (1) a grey road with a white dashed centre line that enters at the top edge about 40% from the left, curves down and to the left, runs down the left part of the picture (about 25-30% from the left) and leaves the bottom edge at the bottom-left; (2) exactly FOUR white tents, each with a small red flag on its peak, all uncoloured: tent A is WEST of the road on the left edge (about 13% from the left, 34% from the top); tent B is east of the road near the top (about 49% from the left, 24% from the top); tent C is east of the road in the middle, directly above the lake with its bottom nearly touching the lake (about 53% from the left, 48% from the top) - it is the tent closest to the lake; tent D is south of the lake, close to the right edge of the road at the bottom (about 47% from the left, 83% from the top); (3) one blue pond (irregular oval, about 45% of the picture width) in the lower middle (centre about 57% from the left, 62% from the top) with FOUR ducks (3 small yellow ducks and 1 white duck) and a few rocks on its rim; (4) many green trees and bushes all around, two yellow-leaved trees at the top, and a few (3 seen) small orange-brown birds in the upper-right trees; the ground is pale yellow. Position summary: tent B is north of tent C; tent A is on the west side of the road; tent D is south of the lake.
unclear: Which tent gets which colour is the student's job (no printed answer); the reading A=blue, C=green, B=purple, D=yellow follows the clues.

belongs_to: 'Write the directions of the following in relation to the girl. Window ____ Bed ____ Cupboard ____ Bedside table ____'
description: Colour illustration of a room drawn in 3-D perspective (not a floor plan): pink walls, pale-grey tiled floor, a black outline frame (about 475 x 300 px on the page). A compass rose (compass rose: a small cream plate with a brown border; a plus-shaped cross of two double-headed arrows; 'N' above, 'S' below, 'W' on the left, 'E' on the right (the E is printed in red, N, W and S in black)) is printed OUTSIDE the frame at its right. Back wall (top of the picture): a blue-grey double-door cupboard at the left-centre (about 21-34% from the left), a wooden barred window in the middle-right of the back wall (about 49-59% from the left) directly above a wooden study table. The girl stands in front of the table near the middle of the picture (about 51% from the left): red dress with light stripes, blue slippers, green hair band, smiling, one hand raised; a blue chair stands to the right of the girl in the picture; the table has a red cup and a sheet of paper. Left wall: a wooden dressing table with a tall mirror and small bottles on it, and a round blue stool in front of it; on the floor at the bottom-left an oval yellow-and-pink patterned rug. Right side: a bed with a curved gold headboard against the right wall (purple star-patterned blanket, lavender sheet, white pillow), a blue-and-teal mat on the floor beside the foot of the bed, and a round wooden bedside table with a red bottle and a glass at the bottom-right corner. On the right wall: a green school bag hanging on a hook and a large dark-grey board in a wooden frame at the top right. If the compass rose is applied to the picture (N = top = back wall): right wall = E, left wall = W, front (viewer side) = S.
unclear: The picture does not mark which wall is north; north = back wall is taken from the compass rose beside it (N at the top).

belongs_to: 'Make a drawing of your room and locate the direction in which different things have been placed in relation to you standing at the centre of the room. Make the direction arrow for your room.' (followed by 4 write-in lines: East, West, North, South)

Nothing is drawn inside it. Below it are four plain write-in lines labelled East, West, North, South (text lines, not a figure).

belongs_to: Street map for the Bus Route text ('The bus will start from the parking area. It will go north and then it will take a right turn onto ____ Road driving in the ____ direction to reach Stop 1 (S1). To reach Stop 2 (S2), it will turn ____ (right/left) onto ____ Road driving in the ____ direction.') and questions (a)-(e): (a) whose houses are east of Jaideep's house, (b) mark the route from Ravi's house to the children's park, (c) which stop is closer to Lali's house, (d) trace Golu's route to the nearest bus stop, (e) in which direction would Prem move to reach Stop 2
description: Top-down cartoon street map in a rounded black frame (about 570 x 480 px), north up. A compass rose (compass rose: a small cream plate with a brown border; a plus-shaped cross of two double-headed arrows; 'N' above, 'S' below, 'W' on the left, 'E' on the right (the E is printed in red, N, W and S in black)) is printed OUTSIDE the frame at the top right. ROADS (dark grey with white dashed centre lines): one unnamed vertical road along the west side of the middle column; the vertical road on the east side of the middle column whose name 'Park Road' is printed rotated (reading downwards) near the top; 'Hospital Road' (horizontal, just below the hospital block, name printed on it); 'Market Road' (horizontal, between the Basketball Court and the Shopping Centre, name printed on it); an unnamed horizontal road below the Shopping Centre and above the Parking; narrow lanes between the house blocks. Side roads on the west side at three heights (between Rohan's and Ravi's blocks, between Ravi's block and the tree block, and at the bottom-left) and on the east side at three heights (between Children's Park and Prem's House, between Prem's and Raju's houses, below Raju's house). BLOCKS with yellow name tags. West column, top to bottom: Lali's House (house with a short drive to the road), Rohan's House, [road], Ravi's House, [road], an unlabelled green block with about 5 trees. Middle column, top to bottom: HOSPITAL (orange tag; blue-roofed building with a red cross; a red round sign 'S1' on a post at the building's right, at the lower edge of the block next to Hospital Road, about 60% across), [Hospital Road], Tinku's House (left) and Golu's House (right) side by side, [lane], an unlabelled blue pond with a few trees around it (left) and Jaideep's House (right, next to Park Road), [lane], Basketball Court (pink tag, grey court with white lines), [Market Road], Shopping Centre (purple tag; 3 small purple-roofed shops and an arch gate; a red round sign 'S2' on a post at the right end of the block next to Park Road), [road], PARKING (orange tag; long grey car park with white bays, entrance on its west side). East column (right of Park Road), top to bottom: Children's Park (name tag at the top; sandy ground with a see-saw, a slide, swings and trees), [side road], Prem's House, [side road], Raju's House, [side road], an unlabelled green block with trees and a brown sandy path. Across Park Road, east of Jaideep's House, are Prem's House (a little higher up, north-east of it) and Raju's House (further down, south-east of it). PRINTED ROUTE (red dashes with arrow-heads, drawn on the road centre lines): a red dashed line runs up the west road with an UP arrow at about 68% and 36% of the map height (measured from the top), turns right (east) onto Hospital Road with a RIGHT arrow at about 37% and 61% of the map width (from the left), turns right (south) onto Park Road with a DOWN arrow at about 39% and 61% of the height, turns right (west) onto the road below the Shopping Centre with a LEFT arrow at about 64% and 42% of the width (from the left), then turns south down the west road beside the Parking, ending in a DOWN arrow at the bottom of the west road at the Parking entrance. A separate red dashed stub enters from the left edge of the map along the bottom-left side road and meets the west road. Stop S1 is on the Hospital Road side (north-east), stop S2 is on the road side next to Park Road at the Shopping Centre (south-east).
unclear: Where the red route begins: the book's text says the bus starts at the parking area and goes north, but the printed arrows on the west road point up and the last arrow at the bottom points down into the parking; the stub entering from the left edge has no arrow. Arrow positions are approximate.
The west vertical road has no printed name.

belongs_to: 'Metro Map: Study the map carefully and answer the questions that follow.' - used by: identify the symbols from the key, what the coloured lines represent, mark Qutb Minar on the Yellow Line and Supreme Court on the Blue Line, and the questions (a)-(d) on the next page (trace routes from Qutb Minar to Supreme Court; Lali's Yellow-then-Magenta idea and where to change again; the route with the fewest stations; the best route to the zoo)
description: Schematic Delhi Metro map in a black dashed frame (about 785 x 530 px), cream background, no compass. Light-blue river band (not labelled): runs down from the top edge at about 62% from the left, bends right in the middle and reaches the bottom edge at about 90% from the left, ending behind the key box. Bottom-left: a yellow-cream dashed box with the title 'Delhi Metro Map' (large black bold, two lines). Bottom-right: the KEYS box (see P05-key-1). Stations are white circles with a black outline on coloured lines; an INTERCHANGE is a rounded capsule containing two coloured dots (one for each line). LINES and labelled stations: YELLOW: runs from the top edge (about 60% from the left) straight down through Kashmeri Gate, New Delhi Stn., Rajiv Chowk, Central Secretariat, INA, Hauz Khas, then bends down-left through Saket and Qutb Minar, goes left through Chattarpur, then down-left to MILLENIUM CITY CENTRE GURUGRAM (end, bottom-left). BLUE: starts at DWARKA SEC 21 (bottom-left), goes up the left edge in a loop, then east through Janakpuri West, Rajouri Garden, Kriti Nagar, then down to Rajiv Chowk, east through Supreme Court to Yamuna Bank; there it splits: one branch goes up-right to Vaishali (end, upper right), the other goes down-right through Mayur Vihar and Botanical Garden to NOIDA City Centre (end, right). RED: enters at the top edge (about 40% from the left), passes the green+red capsule just below, goes down-right and then east along the top third through Kashmeri Gate and an unlabelled red-pink interchange, then up-right to Dilshad Garden (end, top right). GREEN: starts at Mundka (top-left end), runs east along the top edge through Ashok Park (capsule with two green dots) and ends at an unlabelled green-red capsule; a short green branch goes down from Ashok Park to Kriti Nagar. AIRPORT EXPRESS (orange): from DWARKA SEC 21 east through Airport and Delhi Aerocity, then a straight diagonal up-right (2 unlabelled circles) to New Delhi Stn. MAGENTA: from Janakpuri West a long arc down-right through Hauz Khas, east to Kalkaji Mandir, then up-right across the river to Botanical Garden. VIOLET: from Central Secretariat down (unlabelled pink-violet capsule), to Kalkaji Mandir, then down-right to BADARPUR (end, bottom right). PINK: a big ring, cut by the top edge: from the top edge down to Rajouri Garden, then a curve down-right to INA, east along the bottom of the ring through the unlabelled pink-violet capsule, up through Mayur Vihar, then up to the unlabelled blue-pink capsule on the Vaishali branch and on to the unlabelled red-pink capsule near the Red Line, and off the top edge. INTERCHANGE capsules (two dots): Ashok Park (green+green), green+red (unlabelled), Kriti Nagar (blue+green), Rajouri Garden (blue+pink), Janakpuri West (blue+magenta), DWARKA SEC 21 (blue+orange), New Delhi Stn. (orange+yellow), Rajiv Chowk (yellow+blue), Kashmeri Gate (yellow+red), Central Secretariat (yellow+violet), INA (pink+yellow), Hauz Khas (magenta+yellow), Kalkaji Mandir (magenta+violet), Botanical Garden (magenta+blue), Mayur Vihar (blue+pink), Yamuna Bank (blue+blue), unlabelled red+pink, pink+violet and blue+pink - 19 capsules. Supreme Court is an ordinary circle on the Blue Line with a short tick down to its label, between Rajiv Chowk and Yamuna Bank. Qutb Minar is an ordinary circle on the Yellow Line, bottom-centre-left, with the label under it. STATION COUNTS (circles strictly BETWEEN the named stations, counted on the zoomed picture): Yellow Qutb Minar - Saket (0), Saket - Hauz Khas (1 unlabelled), so Qutb Minar to Hauz Khas has 2 between; Hauz Khas - INA 2; INA - Central Secretariat 3; Central Secretariat - Rajiv Chowk 1; so, counting Hauz Khas, INA and Central Secretariat themselves, Yellow Qutb Minar to Rajiv Chowk has 11 stations strictly between. Blue Rajiv Chowk - Supreme Court 2; Supreme Court - Yamuna Bank 1; Yamuna Bank - Mayur Vihar 1; Mayur Vihar - Botanical Garden 5; Botanical Garden - NOIDA City Centre 1; Yamuna Bank - blue-pink capsule 3, capsule - Vaishali 2. Blue Janakpuri West - Rajouri Garden 4; Rajouri Garden - Kriti Nagar 2; Kriti Nagar - Rajiv Chowk 6; Dwarka Sec 21 - Janakpuri West about 12. Magenta Janakpuri West - Hauz Khas 10; Hauz Khas - Kalkaji Mandir 4; Kalkaji Mandir - Botanical Garden 7. Violet Central Secretariat - pink-violet capsule 3; capsule - Kalkaji Mandir 3; Kalkaji Mandir - Badarpur 6. Pink Rajouri Garden - INA 7; INA - pink-violet capsule 1; capsule - Mayur Vihar 3; Mayur Vihar - blue-pink capsule 4. Yellow Qutb Minar - Millenium City Centre Gurugram 8 (first one is Chattarpur). Airport Express Dwarka Sec 21 - New Delhi Stn.: Airport, Delhi Aerocity and 2 unlabelled circles.
unclear: Counts of plain circles were made by eye on enlarged crops; the Green line (about 12 circles plus 2 capsules), the Red line and the top part of the Pink ring were NOT counted fully.
Positions given as percentages are approximate; the capsule total of 19 was counted by eye.
Two unnamed circles on the Airport Express diagonal and several circles on the Blue/Pink lines carry no label in the book.

belongs_to: 'Read the key to the symbols and identify them on the map. What do the different coloured lines represent?' (KEYS box of the Metro Map)
description: A rounded white box with a black outline at the bottom-right of the metro map, with a grey tab 'KEYS' (bold italic) on its top-left corner. Ten numbered entries in three columns. Column 1: 1. a RED line segment labelled 'Red Line'; 2. a YELLOW segment 'Yellow Line'; 3. a BLUE segment 'Blue Line'; 4. an ORANGE segment 'Airport Express Line'. Column 2: 5. a GREEN segment 'Green Line'; 6. a VIOLET (purple) segment 'Violet Line'; 7. a PINK (light pink) segment 'Pink Line'; 8. a MAGENTA (deep pink) segment 'Magenta Line'. Column 3: 9. a plain white circle with a black outline labelled 'Metro Station'; 10. a rounded capsule (black outline) containing a yellow dot and a magenta dot, labelled 'Interchange Line'.

belongs_to: 'Make a map showing the different places in your school. Make a key for the symbols used in the map... A sample map and its key are given below.' (the two key strips left and right of the sample map)
description: Two tall cream strips with a dashed rounded border, hand-drawn black-pencil style, one on each side of the sample map. LEFT strip, top to bottom, 5 symbols: 'Gate' (two small post rectangles with two short diagonal door lines opened in a V, short double lines running out to each side); 'Road' (three stacked horizontal lines: solid, dashed, solid); 'Building' (a rectangle with a double outline divided into two equal squares side by side); 'Tank' (a rounded cog shape, a circle with three notches, with a small circle in the middle); 'Hidden Objects' (a red circle outline). RIGHT strip, top to bottom, 6 symbols: 'Wall' (a thick band hatched with diagonal strokes); 'Fence' (a horizontal line with 5 short vertical tick marks); 'Seat/Bench' (a horizontal rectangle with a block at each end); 'Path' (two solid lines with scattered small dots/commas between them); 'Garden' (3 rows of scalloped arcs, like waves); 'Tree' (a cloud-shaped scalloped outline). Total 11 symbols.

belongs_to: 'A sample map and its key are given below.' - sample school map for the 'Let Us Do' activity (hidden objects marked with red circles; no direction arrow is printed on it)
description: Hand-drawn black-pencil top-down school map on a rounded pale-grey panel (about 680 x 490 px on the page); no compass rose is printed. West (left) side: a road drawn as three vertical lines (solid, dashed, solid) running the full height. Hatched WALL along the whole top and down the upper part of the west side; a GATE gap in the west side about 45-60% down (two small gate posts with the door lines opening outward and a dashed path going out to the road); FENCE (line with tick marks) just inside the wall along the top, down the west side below the gate, along the whole bottom, and along a short stretch at the bottom-right. A dotted PATH forms a rectangular ring inside: it starts at the gate, goes up to the top-left corner, runs east along the top, down the east side and west along the bottom, enclosing a large empty rectangle (open ground) in the middle. A SEAT/BENCH sits on the top branch of the path (about 40-55% across). Inside the open ground at the top-right corner is a square fenced patch with one TREE (cloud shape). At the bottom-left, between the path and the fence, a GARDEN (scalloped rows) bounded by two curved lines. East side: a tall BUILDING block of THREE stacked rectangular rooms (top, middle, bottom; a narrow column about 11% of the panel width) along the east wall of the grounds; a small TANK symbol (cog) drawn in the top room; a small double-lined square (a small structure) just outside the fence at the bottom-right. HIDDEN OBJECTS: exactly FIVE red circles - on the left end of the bench on the top path; at the top-right corner of the tree patch; just west of the tree patch in the open ground; at the top-left end of the garden next to the gate; and at the bottom-right corner of the path/open ground.
unclear: The small square structure at the bottom-right has no key symbol (taken as a small building).

belongs_to: 'To collect food, the ant can only crawl along the dotted lines on the grid. The arrows show the direction in which the ant can move.' + 'Fill in the blanks ... (a) laddoos 2 cm east (given), (b) sugar ____cm ____ direction, (c) bread ____cm ____ ; then ____cm ____, (d) apple ____cm towards ____, then ____cm towards ____, finally ____cm towards ____' + 'Identify other routes to reach the point where apple is located. Which one is the shortest?'
description: Square grid of light-grey squares on a pale background: 11 columns x 11 rows (12 vertical and 12 horizontal grey lines), each square 1 cm (about 42 px), scale mark at the top-right corner: a horizontal dotted double-headed arrow labelled '1cm' (one square wide) and a vertical dotted double-headed arrow labelled '1cm' (one square high, text rotated). A compass rose (compass rose: a small cream plate with a brown border; a plus-shaped cross of two double-headed arrows; 'N' above, 'S' below, 'W' on the left, 'E' on the right (the E is printed in red, N, W and S in black)) sits inside the top-left corner of the grid (about 2 x 2 squares). Number the grid lines 0-11 from the west edge and 0-11 from the north edge. THE ANT (brown, drawn at a line crossing) is at the centre crossing (5, 5) - 5 squares from the west and north edges, 6 from the east and south edges. Four red filled end-dots, each with a picture of the food next to it, and red dashed routes (one arrow-head per straight stretch): (1) LADDOOS (plate of 4 orange laddoos, east of the ant): dashed line from the ant 2 squares EAST to the dot at (7, 5); arrow-head points right. (2) SUGAR (heap of white sugar cubes, north of the ant, top): dashed line from the ant 3 squares NORTH to the dot at (5, 2); arrow-head points up. (3) BREAD (a loaf, bottom-left): dashed line from the ant 3 squares WEST (arrow-head points left) to (2, 5), then 2 squares SOUTH (arrow-head points down) to the dot at (2, 7); the loaf is just below the dot. (4) APPLE (red apple, right-lower area): dashed line from the ant 5 squares SOUTH (arrow-head points down) to (5, 10), then 3 squares EAST (arrow-head points right) to (8, 10), then 2 squares NORTH (arrow-head points up) to the dot at (8, 8); the apple sits just above that dot. So the apple point is 3 squares east and 3 squares south of the ant. The four routes leave the ant along the four different directions: east, north, west, south. Rest of the grid is empty.

section: Locating the Animals in the Zoological Park (Zoo)
belongs_to: Zoo map on a grid: 'Children observe a map of the zoo drawn on a grid... To reach the Panda we start from zero... (1,1)... To reach the tortoise move ____ steps towards east and reach the ____ column. Then move ____ step(s) ____ and reach the first ____. The location of the tortoise is (4,1). What is at (1,4)?' + Q1 (locate the animal at (11,11), (2,6), (6,4), (3,10), (11,3), (10,9)), Q2 (write the position of Lion, Elephant, Tortoise, Deer, Panda, Crocodile), Q3 (place coloured dots at (8,3) red, (2,9) green, (7,3) blue, (3,8) orange, (8,6) black, (6,6) pink)
description: Square green zoo map (about 405 x 405 px) with a thick black ticked border and a grid of black dashed lines: 12 x 12 squares. Grid lines are numbered, not the squares: bottom axis in teal digits '0' (at the bottom-left corner) then '1' to '12' left to right, each digit under its vertical line (line 12 is the right border); left axis in pink digits '1' to '12' printed rotated 90 degrees, bottom to top, each beside its horizontal line (line 12 is the top border); the origin is the bottom-left corner. A point (x, y) = x steps east along the bottom axis, then y steps north. A small compass rose (compass rose: a small cream plate with a brown border; a plus-shaped cross of two double-headed arrows; 'N' above, 'S' below, 'W' on the left, 'E' on the right (the E is printed in red, N, W and S in black)) is printed at the top right of the page next to the section title, outside the grid. ANIMALS (each picture is centred on a line crossing; 16 animals): (1,1) panda (black and white, sitting); (4,1) tortoise; (10,1) crocodile; (3,3) lion (male, with mane); (11,3) monkey sitting on a big tree (the tree spreads around x 10-12, y 2-4); (1,4) coiled snake (cobra); (6,4) elephant (white tusks); (2,6) tiger; (10,6) deer / antelope (small, orange-brown with curved horns); (8,7) tan spotted big cat (cheetah-like); (6,8) hippopotamus in a small blue pond inside the round road; (8,9) giraffe; (10,9) zebra; (3,10) two pink flamingos side by side; (1,11) parrot (green-yellow) on a tree at the top-left; (11,11) toucan (black, big orange beak) on a tree at the top-right. SIGN: an orange rectangle labelled 'ZOO' at the bottom, spanning about x 5.7-8.4, centred at x=7, between y about 0.3 and 0.9; a short cream entrance road runs up from it at x=7 to the bottom horizontal road. CREAM ROADS (not on the grid lines): an outer ring road along the top (y about 11), the west side (x about 1) and the east side (x about 11) with rounded corners; a circular road (roundabout, centre about (5.4, 8), radius about 1.5) around the hippo pond, joined to the top road by a short north spoke at x about 5.5, to the west ring road and to the east ring road by horizontal roads at y about 8, and to a lower horizontal road at y about 5 by a short south spoke at x about 5.5; the y-about-5 road runs from the west road to about x 8.5, where the east ring road curves down-left to join it and then curves down to a bottom horizontal road at y about 2; the bottom road at y about 2 runs from the west road (which turns into it at the bottom-left) to about x 8; a short vertical road at x about 4.4 joins y about 5 and y about 2. No answers or dots are printed on the map.
unclear: Animal positions are read from the centre of each picture on the grid lines (accurate to about 0.1 of a square); the book prints no animal names, so the names are my identification of the pictures (the Q1/Q2 answers it expects are: (11,11) toucan, (2,6) tiger, (6,4) elephant, (3,10) flamingo, (11,3) monkey, (10,9) zebra; lion (3,3), elephant (6,4), tortoise (4,1), deer (10,6), panda (1,1), crocodile (10,1)).
The road layout is approximate (read by eye).
